description: Dropdown context menu triggered by a custom element. Contains TmContextMenuItem children and closes on Escape key press. The menu is a top-layer TmOverlayPanel; it stays the anchored popover at every width unless the host opts into the shared mobile bottom sheet through MobilePresentation.

parameters.name: Trigger
parameters.description: The trigger element that opens the menu.

parameters.name: MobilePresentation
parameters.description: How the menu presents on a narrow viewport. Default Popover: the anchored popover at every width. Auto opts into the shared content-height bottom sheet on a mobile viewport (the anchored popover otherwise). A forced value renders that presentation without measuring (since 2.9.1).

parameters.name: SheetTitle
parameters.description: Title of the sheet header when the menu presents as a bottom sheet. When null (default), the localized TmContextMenu_SheetTitle default is used. The value also names the popover (aria-label) — the menu carries no other accessible name, so a role menu popover is not unnamed (since 2.9.1).

parameters.name: IsOpenChanged
parameters.description: Raised when the menu opens or closes, including a close from the overlay. A host that mounts the menu only while it is open uses this to drop that mount.

parameters.name: TriggerTabIndex
parameters.description: Tab index of the trigger. Defaults to 0: the trigger is the menu's own tab stop. -1 takes it out of the tab order while keeping it pointer-activatable — what a host needs when the trigger sits INSIDE another focusable element that already owns the tab stop (TmKanbanBoard's card owns one roving stop per cell and opens the menu with M / Alt+ArrowDown, so a second stop would double the cell's tab stops). null omits the attribute.

parameters.name: TriggerAriaLabel
parameters.description: Accessible name of the emulating trigger. Null (default) keeps the trigger unnamed — use it when the trigger fragment itself carries a visible or accessible label; a nameless role=button div with an icon-only fragment is unnamed to a reader (since 2.12.0).

parameters.name: AsChild
parameters.description: Renders no emulating trigger at all: the wrapper becomes presentational and the host's own trigger element inside the Trigger fragment receives the menu-button semantics from the cascaded ContextMenuTriggerContext (aria-haspopup, aria-expanded via IsOpen, activation via ToggleAsync). Use it whenever the trigger fragment holds a real interactive control — a div[role=button] wrapped around a button is a nested interactive element (since 2.12.0).

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class for the root element.

examples.title: Context menu with actions
examples.code:
<TmContextMenu>
    <Trigger>
        <TmButton Variant="ButtonVariant.Ghost" Size="ButtonSize.Sm">...</TmButton>
    </Trigger>
    <ChildContent>
        <TmContextMenuItem Label="Edit" Icon="edit" OnClick="EditItem" />
        <TmContextMenuItem Label="Duplicate" Icon="copy" OnClick="DuplicateItem" />
        <TmContextMenuItem IsDivider="true" />
        <TmContextMenuItem Label="Delete" Icon="trash-2" IsDangerous="true" OnClick="DeleteItem" />
    </ChildContent>
</TmContextMenu>

examples.title: Opt-in mobile bottom sheet
examples.code:
<TmContextMenu MobilePresentation="PanelPresentation.Auto" SheetTitle="Row actions">
    <Trigger>
        <TmButton Variant="ButtonVariant.Ghost" Size="ButtonSize.Sm">Actions</TmButton>
    </Trigger>
    <ChildContent>
        <TmContextMenuItem Label="Edit" Icon="edit" OnClick="EditItem" />
    </ChildContent>
</TmContextMenu>

examples.title: AsChild trigger (2.12.0) — the host's own button owns the semantics
examples.code:
// In a host component with [CascadingParameter] ContextMenuTriggerContext? Menu:
<TmContextMenu AsChild="true">
    <Trigger>
        <button type="button" aria-haspopup="menu" aria-expanded="@(Menu?.IsOpen == true)" @onclick="@(() => Menu?.ToggleAsync())">⋯</button>
    </Trigger>
    <ChildContent>
        <TmContextMenuItem Label="Edit" OnClick="EditItem" />
    </ChildContent>
</TmContextMenu>
